retrieved.heading: What this endorsement does
retrieved.text:
Adds expense reimbursement coverage for an insured who is the victim of an **identity fraud
event** or a **personal cyber event**. This is an expense-reimbursement coverage, not a
liability coverage.

retrieved.heading: Deductible
retrieved.text: A **$250 deductible** applies per identity fraud or cyber event.

retrieved.heading: Claim handling note
retrieved.text:
Identity fraud claims are handled by the **Specialty Lines desk**, not the property team.
First contact target is **two business days**. A completed **Identity Theft Affidavit** and
the police report reference number are required before any expense is reimbursed.
Ransomware claims must be escalated to the Cyber duty manager **before** any payment is
discussed with the insured.

retrieved.heading: Conditions
retrieved.text:
- The insured must **report the event to the police, the bank, and the affected
  institutions within 30 days** of discovery.
- A **ransomware payment is only reimbursed** where Meridian Mutual gave **prior written
  consent** and where paying was the only reasonable means of recovering the data.
- Devices must have had **commercially available anti-malware software installed and
  current** at the time of the event, for the cyber portion only. This condition does not
  apply to the identity fraud portion.
- Coverage applies to events **first discovered during the policy period**, even where the
  underlying fraud began before inception, provided the policy has been continuously in
  force for at least **12 months**.

retrieved.heading: 3. Deductible application
retrieved.text:
The deductible is applied **once per occurrence**, not once per coverage. Where an
endorsement carries its own deductible, that deductible replaces the base deductible for
the portion of the loss falling under the endorsement:

- Water backup (HO-2026-01): **$500**, replacing the base $1,000
- Service line (HO-2026-02): **$500**, replacing the base $1,000
- Equipment breakdown (HO-2026-03): **$500**, replacing the base $1,000
- Scheduled property (HO-2026-04): **no deductible**
- Identity fraud (HO-2026-07): **$250**

Where a single occurrence triggers both a base-form loss and an endorsement loss, apply the
**base deductible once to the base-form portion** and the endorsement deductible once to
the endorsement portion. Do not apply the base deductible to the endorsement portion as
well.

question: For claim [CLAIM_NO] (claimant [CLAIMANT]), the freezer and the basement both flooded. Does he pay two deductibles?

retrieved.heading: My freezer failed and I lost all the food.
retrieved.text:
Food spoilage is covered up to **$1,000** under endorsement HO-2026-03, but only where the
spoilage followed a covered **breakdown** of the freezer or of the electrical supply
equipment. Spoilage from an off-premises power cut with no equipment damage is not covered,
because power failure away from the premises is excluded by the base form.

retrieved.heading: Deductibles
retrieved.text:
The base all-perils deductible is **$1,000 per occurrence**, applied to Section I property
losses only. No deductible applies to Coverage E or Coverage F.

A separate **windstorm or hail deductible of 2% of the Coverage A limit** applies in
designated coastal territories, as shown in the Declarations. Where both the all-perils and
the windstorm deductible could apply to a single occurrence, only the **larger** of the two
is deducted.

retrieved.heading: My basement flooded after heavy rain. Am I covered?
retrieved.text:
It depends on how the water got in. If water **backed up through a drain or sewer**, or a
**sump pump overflowed**, and you have endorsement HO-2026-01, you are covered up to
$10,000 (or $25,000 if you chose the higher limit) with a $500 deductible. If **surface
water flowed in** from outside — over the ground, through a window well, or from a river or
storm surge — that is **flood**, and flood is not covered by any endorsement in this pack.
Flood cover must be bought separately.

retrieved.heading: The pipe from my house to the street broke. Who pays?
retrieved.text:
If the break is on **your side** of the utility connection point and you have endorsement
HO-2026-02, we pay up to $15,000 including excavation and reinstating your lawn or
driveway, with a $500 deductible. If the break is on the **utility's side**, the utility is
responsible and we would decline and refer it to them.
